name: Standard Scramble (Switchback / Klahhane Ridge approach)
approach: From the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center parking lot (end of Hurricane Ridge Road, ~17 mi south of Port Angeles via Race St/Hwy 101), start on the paved High Ridge Trail at the east end of the lot. At about 0.3 mi bear toward Sunrise Point/Klahhane Ridge Trail and continue along open, exposed subalpine ridge (alternating meadow and pocket forest) for roughly 2.5 mi to an unsigned junction where a distinct, unmaintained 'climbers trail' splits left (west) off the maintained Klahhane Ridge Trail — this is the start of the true scramble route (sometimes mapped as the Mount Angeles Summit Climbers Trail). A shorter, steeper alternative start exists directly off Hurricane Ridge Road at the Switchback Trail (~mile marker in the last few miles before the visitor center), which gains about 700-800 ft in 0.6 mi to meet the Mount Angeles Trail higher up, cutting off some of the ridge walk. From the climbers-trail junction, the primitive use trail climbs steeply through rocky meadows and thinning forest on the peak's west side — this final push is only about 0.6 mi but does roughly 800 of the route's 2,100 total feet of gain (average grade ~27%, max ~42%), topping out around 6,000 ft at the base of the summit block/gully. Route-finding note from on-the-ground reports: don't scramble the first notch you reach — stay on the faint boot path traversing higher to the actual summit gully. From there, most parties scramble the right/east side of the final block, which is loose, fractured 'rotten' rock (the same line the descent explicitly avoids downclimbing) with only brief but exposed final moves to the true summit (6,454 ft). There is no reliable water past the visitor center (which has a seasonal contact station with restrooms/potable water) — carry all you need. Key hazards: lingering rotten/consolidated snow choking the summit notch/gully well into July and August even in normal years, loose scree and fractured, rockfall-prone rock on the upper scramble, and sustained exposure along the open ridge crest.

climbing_route.label: Climbers' trail up the west side
climbing_route.notes: At the unsigned junction roughly 2.5 mi along the Klahhane Ridge Trail, a distinct unmaintained climbers' trail splits left (west) — the start of the true scramble. The primitive use trail climbs steeply through rocky meadows and thinning forest on the peak's west side: only about 0.6 mi but roughly 800 of the route's 2,100 ft of gain (average grade ~27%, max ~42%), topping out around 6,000 ft at the base of the summit block/gully. Sustained exposure along the open ridge crest below.

climbing_route.label: Traverse to the summit gully
climbing_route.notes: Do not scramble the first notch you reach — stay on the faint boot path traversing higher to the actual summit gully. Rotten, consolidated snow can choke the summit notch/gully well into July and August even in normal years.

climbing_route.label: Final summit block
climbing_route.notes: Most parties scramble the right/east side of the final block on loose, fractured 'rotten' rock — the same line the descent explicitly avoids downclimbing. Brief but exposed final moves to the true summit at 6,454 ft. Loose scree and rockfall-prone rock throughout the upper scramble.

approach_variants.name: Klahhane Ridge climbers' trail from Hurricane Ridge
approach_variants.notes: Paved path off the east end of the visitor centre lot, then open subalpine ridge for about two and a half miles to an unsigned split. A shorter, steeper start climbs from the Switchback Trail on the road below and joins higher up. Nothing dependable to drink past the visitor centre — carry it all.
hazards: Fractured, rotten rock on the summit block with holds that break
Rockfall funnelling down the crux gully onto anyone below
Rotten snow choking the summit notch into July and August
Exposed Class 3 moves with a fall of well over a hundred feet
Fast-building afternoon storms on a fully exposed ridge
approach_variants.baseFinding: The climbers' path leaves the maintained Klahhane Ridge Trail at an unsigned fork roughly 2.3 miles out: bear left and uphill to the west, where the maintained tread carries on right along the ridge toward Victor Pass and Lake Angeles. From the fork the primitive path climbs rocky meadow on the peak's west side and does about eight hundred of the day's feet in a little over half a mile, topping out near 6,000 ft in a scree bowl beneath the summit block. The identification that matters here is which notch, and it catches people every season: do not scramble the first notch you reach. The boot path keeps traversing higher and the gully that goes is further along, directly beneath the true summit. Stay on the worn tread climber's-left of the open scree fan rather than going straight up the fan itself, which is the rockfall funnel. You are at the base when the meadow ends and you are standing on dirty, fractured ledges with a roughly forty-foot exposed step above you. If the ground has levelled off or you are back on maintained tread heading toward Lake Angeles, you have overshot.

bivy.name: Heart o' the Hills campground
bivy.notes: This is the staging base for Mount Angeles and it is a staging base only — it is a few miles up the Hurricane Ridge road from Port Angeles, and no part of the climb passes through it. The scramble itself starts from a pull-out around mile 15 on that road, where the Switchback trail gains about 700 ft in six-tenths of a mile to its junction with the trail from Hurricane Ridge, then about half a mile west along that trail and a spur onto the unmaintained final ridge — exposed walking and class 3 on loose fractured rock to the 6,454 ft summit. It is a day trip for a fit party, so this camp exists for the group that starts late, gets weathered off, or wants to be at the trailhead at first light. Read the road before you count on it: in winter the Hurricane Ridge road is plowed and open only Friday through Sunday plus a few holiday dates, with uphill traffic released from mid-morning, and it closes without notice in bad weather. Recent seasons have also brought midweek closures for utility work in the weeks after Memorial Day, so check the current schedule rather than assuming summer means open. Because there are no reservations, arrive early on a summer weekend.
bivy.water: Drinking water on tap, flush toilets and rubbish collection through the season
bivy.permit: No wilderness permit — frontcountry campground, nightly fee paid on site, park entrance fee applies. Fires permitted in the provided rings unless a seasonal ban is in force, which happens most late summers on this peninsula.
bivy.capacity: Around 105 single-family sites in old growth, taking tents and rigs up to about 24 ft with a few longer; first-come, first-served with no reservations

approach_variants.notes: A steep, short trail from the Hurricane Ridge Road up to the Klahhane Ridge trail, then the same climbers' path to the summit.

approachLogistics.trailhead: Heather Park Trailhead (Heart O' the Hills)

approach_variants.notes: The long way from low on the Hurricane Ridge Road: the Heather Park trail climbs around the west side of the peak to join the climbers' path.

waypoints.name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (High Ridge Trailhead)
waypoints.note: Start at the east end of the Hurricane Ridge parking lot on the paved Cirque Rim path onto High Ridge Trail; restrooms/potable water here in summer, none beyond this point.
waypoints.directions: Drive Hurricane Ridge Road about 17 miles south from Port Angeles — Race Street off Highway 101 — to the road's end at the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center, around 5,250 ft. Park in the visitor center lot and start at its east end, on the paved Cirque Rim path onto the High Ridge Trail. Come early, since parking here fills. The seasonal contact station has restrooms and potable water, and it is the last of either — there is no reliable water anywhere past the lot.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Point spur junction
waypoints.note: Optional 0.2-mi dead-end spur to a panoramic overlook; stay on the main High Ridge/Sunrise Ridge Nature Trail toward Klahhane Ridge to continue.
waypoints.directions: From the east end of the visitor center lot, follow the paved High Ridge Trail uphill to the junction with the short spur to Sunrise Point; stay on the main trail toward Klahhane Ridge.

waypoints.name: Morse Creek valley overlook spur
waypoints.note: Short spur trail to a viewpoint over the Morse Creek/Elwha drainages; roughly 800 ft of the day's climbing is behind you and the trail steepens above.

waypoints.name: Mount Angeles trail fork (Klahhane Ridge split)
waypoints.note: Bear left to stay on the climbers' path toward the Mount Angeles summit block; the right fork continues along Klahhane Ridge toward Victor Pass/Lake Angeles and is not the summit route.

waypoints.name: Exposed Class 3 crux step below summit block
waypoints.note: ~40-ft exposed move on loose, rotten rock near the top of the scree bowl where the boot path fades into talus; a fall here could exceed 100 ft, many parties spot or rope this step.

waypoints.name: Mount Angeles summit
waypoints.note: True summit (6,454 ft), high point of the Klahhane Ridge/Hurricane Ridge area with views over the Elwha Valley, Port Angeles, and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
